thread:
Marcus: hey @people-ops — divorce finalized today. need to remove my ex-spouse from medical/dental as of 06/15. can we backdate removal and get premium refund? also does ex get COBRA and what do i need to upload?

Nina: sorry to hear that, Marcus. Congrats on getting paperwork sorted. Short answers: 1) we can remove a dependent retro to the divorce effective date if you provide the final divorce decree showing the date. 2) COBRA: ex-spouse is typically eligible as a qualified beneficiary and will have a separate election window. 3) refunds: payroll/benefits will reconcile premiums — options below.

Marcus: thanks. i already have the signed decree PDF and the judge-signed date is 2024-06-15. i uploaded the decree to the secure portal now. what happens next?

benefits-bot: Automated: upload received. Please reply here with "uploaded" after adding files to the portal. Allowed filenames: dependent_docs/<your-lastname>_divorce_decree_<yyyymmdd>.pdf.

Marcus: uploaded as dependent_docs/Lopez_divorce_decree_20240620.pdf — portal shows timestamp 2024-06-20 but decree date is 2024-06-15.

Nina: got it. We'll start a QLE removal request and ask the carrier to use 2024-06-15 as the termination date. Benefits will also trigger a COBRA election packet for your ex-spouse (they will receive direct instructions via mail/email on how to elect).

Derek: payroll note: once benefits approves retro removal we reconcile premium overpayments. Two common outcomes: A) direct refund on next payroll (one-time credit) or B) credit applied to upcoming premiums. If the refund amount is small we usually credit it; if larger we can issue a net check. Marcus, which do you prefer? Reply "refund" or "credit". If you need installments we can split across two pay cycles if you say "split-2" before payroll cutoff.

Marcus: refund please. if refund needs extra approval that's fine. also will this affect my HSA contributions and dependent care FSA elections mid-year?

Nina: HSA: you can update HSA contributions mid-year on a QLE if eligibility changes (e.g., you lose family coverage). Dependent care FSA: you can decrease elections if the dependent is no longer eligible. We'll add those changes when processing the QLE. Please list any elections you want changed.

Marcus: ok drop spouse from coverage, keep myself and kids. lower dependent-care FSA to $0 (kids now with ex). keep HSA unchanged for now.

Derek: noted. We'll process the payroll refund and the FSA change after benefits finalizes the carrier termination. Expect the refund on the next payroll run; if the refund exceeds $1,000 we'll coordinate a net check per payroll policy and DM you.

benefits-bot: Next steps: benefits will file the carrier termination (using 2024-06-15), send COBRA packet to ex-spouse, and confirm changes here within 2 business days. Payroll will confirm refund method and amount once benefits confirms termination.

Nina: thanks @Marcus. closing loop when carrier confirms termination and payroll posts the refund. if ex-spouse needs proof of COBRA eligibility for 60-day election window, direct them to the COBRA contact in the packet.

Marcus: thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround.
